extracted.intended_audience: journalists, researchers, and general readers seeking information about the White House Correspondents' Association and its awards
extracted.subtask_description: A factual encyclopedia entry describing the White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA), its roles (seating/credentialing), the annual dinner, and the various journalism awards the WHCA administers or has administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHCA membership criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for membership is made online and granted by the association on the basis of criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes membership is granted on the basis of criteria but does not list those criteria. Historically the WHCA handled credentialing, access to the president, and physical conditions in the White House press briefing rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seating assignment in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The WHCA is responsible for assigning the seats and the standing room in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room in the White House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though the press office issues passes, the correspondents' association decides who sits where. The board of directors assigns news sources to positions (which change about each 3–4 years). Most media providers have their own seat, but some share seats. The association usually publishes the seating chart on its website whenever a new one comes into effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aldo Beckman Memorial Award — overall excellence in White House coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes 'a correspondent who personifies the journalistic excellence and personal qualities of Aldo Beckman' for overall excellence in White House coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established in 1981 and described as 'one of journalism's most prestigious awards.' Past recipients listed as examples of the type of excellence honored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award for Excellence in Presidential News Coverage Under Deadline Pressure (Merriman Smith Memorial Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established in 1970 as the Merriman Smith Memorial Award for outstanding examples of deadline reporting; recognizes excellence in presidential news coverage under deadline pressure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award specifically honors outstanding deadline reporting about the presidency. The article notes the award was renamed in 2022 and provides many examples of past recipients across print and broadcast categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Katharine Graham Award for Courage and Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: A $10,000 prize to 'recognize an individual or newsgathering team for coverage of subjects and events of significant national or regional importance in line with the human and professional qualities exemplified by the late Katharine Graham.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debuted in 2020. The entry gives the stated prize purpose and links it to Graham's human and professional qualities; winners are listed for recent years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award for Excellence in Presidential News Coverage by Visual Journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: $1,000 'award recognizes a video or photojournalist for uniquely covering the presidency from a journalistic standpoint, either at the White House or in the field.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible work 'could be breaking news, a scheduled event or feature coverage.' Debuted in 2020; winners and example works are listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edgar A. Poe Memorial Award — excellence in news coverage (discontinued)
rubrics_metrics.description: The award honored excellence in news coverage of subjects and events of significant national or regional importance to the American people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded by Newhouse Newspapers and presented from 1990 to 2019; replaced by the Katharine Graham Award and the Visual Journalists award. Notable past winners illustrate the type of work recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raymond Clapper Memorial Award — distinguished Washington reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 'to a journalist or team for distinguished Washington reporting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented from 1944 to 2003 (usually at the WHCA dinner); in 2004 the award passed to the Scripps Howard National Journalism Awards and was presented under that program until being discontinued in 2011. Notable past winners are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: WHCA awards dating convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Award years represent the date the work was published/broadcast, which is always one year before the prize was awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains how award years are listed in the article and clarifies that the year attached to an award item refers to the work's publication/broadcast year, not the ceremony year.
